tutorial.title: How to access one HTML element
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to access one HTML element to store it in JS,

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've already seen that we can use JavaScript variables, like element here, to store game HUD elements.

Make sure to pick const, followed by element.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
And we saw that we can use getElementById to access the HTML element with the health id.

Make sure to pick document, followed by .getElementById, and finally ("health");.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
But let's practice that a bit more! We can access the text of the HUD through the variable name, with .innerHTML.

Make sure to pick element, followed by ., and finally innerHTML.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also use the variable to update the HUD content, by adding = and the new value "Health: 0".

Make sure to pick element followed by . and then innerHTML, =, "Health: 0".

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we store the element we're accessing through document.getElementById()?

Using a variableWe can't store it since it's not a value

Using a variable.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which element does the hud variable contain?

The p elementThe h3 element

The p element.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this code display in the console?

Level 1: The Forestdocument.getElementById("level")

Level 1: The Forest.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's the text of the h2 element when the webpage displays?

"Boss Fight!""Level Start"

"Boss Fight!".

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a variable to store the ul element.

Make sure to pick itemList followed by = and then document, ., getElementById, (, "items", ).

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Save the heading into the variable by assembling the code.

Make sure to pick title =, followed by document, and finally .getElementById("status");.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the paragraph's text by assembling the code inside the display statement.

Make sure to pick quest, followed by ., and finally innerHTML =.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Update the shop's name using the title variable and the .innerHTML instruction.

Make sure to pick title, followed by ., and finally innerHTML.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've seen how to use id to query HTML elements.

But what if the element doesn't have an id? Let's learn how to query specific selectors in our game UI.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we want to retrieve an individual HTML element, we can use the querySelector() method from document.

Make sure to pick querySelector.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
To select a specific element, we add a selector inside parentheses.

We can use an HTML tag, like the p tag if we want to get the game status text.

Make sure to pick p.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
Once we've stored the element in a variable, we can change it. Here, we're using the innerHTML property to change its content.

Complete the code and press the button to see that querySelector also works!

Make sure to pick el followed by . and then innerHTML, =.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
querySelector() works with all selectors, like tags, classes, and IDs. If we're looking for an ID, we add the # at the beginning.

Make sure to pick #, followed by hud.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we're looking for a class, we have to add . at the beginning.

Make sure to pick ., followed by hud.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
querySelector() only retrieves the first element it finds.

So, if we have two elements with the same tag or class, we only access the first one.

Make sure to pick <h3>, followed by Level 1, and finally </h3>.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the querySelector() method access?

Only the first HTML element that matches its searchAll HTML elements that match its search

Only the first HTML element that matches its search.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which h3 element does the respawn() function change?

The first h3 elementThe second h3 element

The first h3 element.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which h3 element does the respawn() function change?

The one with the boss IDThe first h3 element

The one with the boss ID.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What selectors does the querySelector() method work with?

Any selectors, including tags, classes, or ID'sIt only works with tags or ID

Any selectors, including tags, classes, or ID's.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code where we're trying to access an element with a specific class?

The . is missing from the class selectorThe # is missing from the class selector

The . is missing from the class selector.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code querySelector() as a method for document.

Make sure to pick document followed by . and then querySelector, (, ).

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the selector for the p element inside parentheses.

Make sure to pick ", followed by p, and finally ".

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the querySelector to access the element with the #update ID.

Make sure to type #update.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the .loot class.

Make sure to pick ., followed by loot.

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the selector to change the text of the second h3 element.

Make sure to pick ., followed by warning.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
We know querySelector() gets the first element it finds. That can be a problem if the element we want is later in the code.

Code .hud and then press the button to see how only the first element with that class changes.

Make sure to pick ., followed by hud.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
If several elements share a class, like .hud here, we can specify its tag.

We specify p.hud inside parentheses to select the paragraph with the .hud class.

Make sure to pick p, followed by ., and finally hud.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also look for an element that has multiple classes. Before we can see that work, add the class name active to the second paragraph.

Make sure to type active.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
To access an element with two classes, we include them together. Here, it is .hud.active or .active.hud.

Now we do not need to specify the HTML tag because there is only one element with those two classes.

Make sure to pick ., followed by active.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
querySelector is very powerful and we can use it to access any specific element in a game UI.

Make sure to pick querySelector followed by ( and then ".wave.info", ).

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is wrong with this code if we want to access a p element of class hud?

It should be p.hudIt should be p#hud

It should be p.hud.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we select an element with multiple classes?

One class name after another with a . before eachOne class after another with a space in between

One class name after another with a . before each.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which p element does the querySelector() method access?

The third p elementThe second p element

The third p element.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
When do we use the querySelector() method?

Anytime we want to access elements with specific selectorsWe only use it when an element does not have an ID

Anytime we want to access elements with specific selectors.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the .boss selector to access the right element.

Make sure to pick ., followed by boss.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code p.credits to change the text of the last paragraph.

Make sure to pick p, followed by ., and finally credits.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
Select the paragraph element by coding p.boss.

Make sure to type p.boss.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
Select the paragraph element by coding the p.alert.boss.

Make sure to pick p followed by . and then alert, ., boss.
